_about: Visual references for STYLE.md. Each id matches a <!-- ref:id --> marker. Times are seconds in the reference; crops are [x0, y0, x1, y1] in the 736x370 active picture. build_pack.py renders these from the reference video into refs/pack/ (gitignored).

overview-contact.caption: The whole reference at one frame per second (0–50 s). One continuous journey through about 18 worlds.

style-board.caption: Style board: twelve representative frames. Paper-puppet people, lit tabletop worlds, torn-paper tags, warm print grade.

format-letterbox.caption: Format: a 2:1 picture letterboxed inside a 16:9 file.

comp-depth-planes.caption: Four depth planes: soft cropped foreground props, the hero cut-out, the set piece, the backdrop. A tag sits in 3D space.

comp-proscenium.caption: Proscenium staging: frontal, eye level, hero centred, like a stage or shop window.

comp-tags.caption: Every torn-paper tag in the piece (crops, enlarged): terracotta, red, mustard, olive and cobalt paper; white or dark sans-serif text; rotated 5–15°; sitting in 3D space.

comp-hierarchy.caption: Visual hierarchy in one frame: the eye goes 1 face (or its replacement), 2 the loudest accent, 3 the tag, 4 soft foreground, 5 backdrop.

art-layers.caption: World-building layers, one row per layer.

art-gags.caption: The gags: one deadpan swap per world, held 1–2 s.

items: toy props: cube, piggy bank, handheld console
art-era.caption: Era prop vocabulary (the reference's era is 1999). Pick one coherent era or theme per piece.

texture-materials.caption: Materials, cropped and enlarged. The texture comes from real materials, not from grain or filters.

items: saturated accents on a muted base
grade-examples.caption: The grade across very different worlds: warm mean, cream (never clipped) highlights, brown shadows.

tr-T1.caption: T1 occluder wipe: a foreground object fills the lens for 1–2 images and the new world is behind it.

tr-T2.caption: T2 tear / peel: the surface facing the camera tears, or its paper layers slide apart.

rows: eye closes, opens on next world
tr-T3.caption: T3 portal dive: push into an opening (eye, mouth); it closes or darkens, then opens on the next world.

rows: pull out of a button eye
pull out of a cassette reel window
tr-T4.caption: T4 reverse portal: pulling back reveals the last world was inside a round object.

rows: wall of papers becomes the floor
tr-T5.caption: T5 plane flip: a tilt turns a wall into a floor or table.

tr-T6.caption: T6 whip smear: 1–2 smeared images hide the cut.

tr-T7.caption: T7 crash-in: a dark smear, then a big object slams in and settles.

tr-T8.caption: T8 crumple away: an object crumples into paper and is carried off.

tr-T9.caption: T9 carry-over element: the koi swims on through the crash, the top-down map and the peel.

tr-T10.caption: T10 substitution gag: an in-shot swap, not a scene change.

cadence-frames.caption: Eight consecutive frames (24 fps file). Every image is held for two frames: animation on twos, even during camera moves.

rows: portal dive: exponential ease-in, cut at peak
title slam: ease-in, impact hold, overshoot (on ones)
ease-strips.caption: The five measured move types, matching the ease-profile graphs above (left to right is time).

rows: hold: ~0.9% of width per image, reads smooth
smear: over 6% per image, used only as a smear
smooth-examples.caption: Step size vs smoothness: consecutive new images at three speeds.

rows: anticipation: near-still macro, then the slide
follow-through: tag swings in and sways
secondary action: koi behind the crash
parallax: globes faster than the set
cloning: one raised hand becomes a crowd
principles-strips.caption: Animation principles as the reference uses them (consecutive new images).

items: bear the size of a church
pr-exaggeration.caption: Exaggeration through scale, not motion.

sound-events.caption: What the picture is doing at each sound event (the score hits the action).

style-frames.caption: Candidate style frames to attach as @image1 (palette, materials, light and paper rendering only; never cast, text or composition).

scene-thumbs.caption: One frame per row of the scene map.
